headline: Brigham nurses set Oct. 14 date for open-ended strike
dek: The union has given Mass General Brigham 10 days’ notice, but says a contract agreement could still avert the planned walkout.
body: Nurses at Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston have scheduled an open-ended strike to begin at 7 a.m. on Oct. 14 if they do not reach a contract agreement with Mass General Brigham. The Massachusetts Nurses Association, which represents about 4,000 Brigham nurses, said it delivered the hospital the legally required 10-day notice on Oct. 2. A [Boston 25 News report](https://cmg-cmg-tv-10020-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/4000-brigham-nurses-set-strike-date-heres-when-they-could-walk-off-job/OC3KYWUW2JDWBII6X2FQBKLRUU/) independently reported the planned date and notice. The union says the work stoppage would continue until the parties reach a deal.

The date is a new escalation in a dispute that had previously produced only a strike authorization. Nurses voted 2,986 to 215 on Sept. 24 to authorize an indefinite walkout, according to the union and Boston 25. That vote did not itself take nurses off the job; the notice gives patients, the hospital and negotiators a specific deadline while leaving open the possibility that an agreement could avert the strike.

The planned action follows a one-day nurse strike on July 8 and a four-day lockout that followed, according to the union’s notice and the Boston 25 report. The MNA is classifying the possible walkout as an unfair-labor-practice strike and says nurses have filed multiple labor complaints against the hospital since July. Those are union allegations, not findings made in this article; the hospital’s public update says it considers the parties at an impasse and is willing to return when it sees progress on key issues.

The disagreement covers both economics and how care is staffed. The union says it wants a stronger permanent nursing workforce, limits on Mass General Brigham’s reliance on temporary nurses, affordable health insurance and meaningful plan choices. It also says the two sides remain apart over compensation. Those demands matter beyond the bargaining unit because they touch staffing continuity and the experience of patients receiving care at one of Boston’s major hospitals.

Mass General Brigham’s own [strike information page](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/about/brigham-and-womens-hospital/nursing/mna-updates) says the parties have bargained since November 2025, held 25 sessions and reached 16 tentative agreements, with significant economic differences still unresolved. The hospital says the last session was Aug. 11, when management told the union it was at an impasse. It says its current proposal includes yearly 5% raises within a 20-step pay scale, extra pay or bonuses for nurses at the top step, continued extra-shift pay, career support and health benefits.

The hospital also says Brigham will remain open if a strike begins. Mass General Brigham says it has arranged for skilled, experienced nurses to join existing care teams, with orientation before their first shifts, and advises patients to keep appointments unless their care team contacts them. The hospital asks patients with questions or rescheduling needs to contact their provider’s office and allow extra time for traffic near the facility. The MNA says it remains willing to negotiate and is urging management to return to the table before Oct. 14.

The immediate question is whether the 10-day notice produces renewed negotiations or an agreement before the deadline. If the strike proceeds, the notice has no set end date: the union says it would last until a contract is reached, while the hospital says nurses could return only after both sides agree on a return-to-work plan and timing. For Boston patients, the scheduled date turns a labor dispute into a concrete planning issue, but it is not yet proof that a walkout will occur.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Brigham Nurses Set Oct. 14 Strike Date
seoDescription: Brigham and Women’s nurses have given Mass General Brigham 10 days’ notice of a possible open-ended strike starting Oct. 14.
